column10: the keys are parsed into NodeConf and read by nothing outside the configuration module, so max-message-consumers leaves the effective dispatch bound at the hardcoded 1024 and the keepalive group leaves no http2 or tcp keepalive anywhere, while defaults.conf's longest comment tells operators to tune the first one

exploratory_deploy reads the highest-height block and an arbitrary hash from that height, so the no-hash default is the non-finalized chain tip; commit 63c535c6d reverted the fix R19 records as landed and never touched the register, so the row is false of this tree and nothing tracks the defect

create_block selects every valid pooled deploy and turns the count into a u8 for the randomness seed, so a pool of 256 makes the seed conversion fail before any state work and the proposer can never produce a block; the pool cap of 10_000 and the per-block capacity of 255 are set in different places

read in full — the enum, is_valid, Display, and the ALL ratchet with its three tests — while adding C120's status variant, and it holds no defect. Basis for clearing rather than deferring: the module is a closed vocabulary whose completeness is enforced by construction (ALL's length is checked by the type system and its test forces every variant to render a distinct message), so "a variant with no message" cannot survive a compile. Not read: the callers that turn a status into a refusal are separate rows (casper/src/multi_parent_casper.rs, casper/src/blocks/block_processor.rs)

the ledger is a bare KeyValueTypedStore keyed by hash(txn_id) with plain get and put, which is the store the non-atomic check-then-act above runs on; it also has no cap and no expiry, so a scanner walks it in full

run() reads the coordinator ledger, decides there is no record, then writes one, with no lock, no per-txn_id serialization and no compare-and-set on the durable store, so two concurrent calls for one txn_id both open the transaction and the record can describe effects that were never applied
the checkpoint replay is where the slash set is checked against this node's own DAG metadata, because the justification hashes carry no slashable flag
block validation replayed a peer's Slash without re-deriving who the block's justifications hold responsible; the rule is shared with the proposer here
discovery was plaintext and unauthenticated on a public port, and its messages named a sender nothing checked; it now serves over the transport's mutual TLS and binds the sender to the certificate

find_and_connect awaits connect() for every peer in the routing table serially with no cap, and MAX_CONNECTIONS is applied to the result rather than inside the loop, so one peer's fabricated table stalls the RP loop for hours; the verifier assessed this as a faithful port of the Scala shape, so it may belong in the deviation register rather than as a defect
the stream handler's only byte cap was per-stream while the stream count multiplied it; the aggregate budget and the unary transport decode cap both land in this receiver

verify_bytes hands the caller's data to verify_prehash, which truncates anything longer than 32 bytes to its leftmost 32, so the rho secp256k1Verify contract returns a verdict over the message's prefix rather than the message; demonstrated by verifying msg32 concatenated with an unsigned suffix

BlockMetadata::from_proto hard-codes slashable:false and the proto has no such field, so every metadata a validator can read loses the flag on the store round-trip and the C110 slash rule has no reachable input; the whole justified-confiscation mechanism is inert
the charge and the refund are computed here from wire-supplied phlo fields; both returned a bare i64 whose sign was unchecked, so a negative limit produced a usable amount

a malformed config file is silently truncated because the hocon loader is non-strict, so the node runs on defaults for every key after the first syntax error with no error and no log line; the same module silently substitutes the default profile for an unknown --profile, moving the data directory

model.rs and defaults.conf both cite spec/AUDIT.md C315, which is not an allocated row, and the pointer check cannot see it because pointer_sources is built from spec/*.md and spec/Rchain/*.lean only, so the cross-reference discipline is unenforced outside spec/

no signal handler is installed anywhere in the workspace and the binary is PID 1 in the container, so SIGTERM is delivered and discarded and every stop burns the grace period before SIGKILL; there is no graceful shutdown path, so LMDB environments are not closed and in-flight work is killed mid-flight
the admin HTTP server bound api-server.host with an unauthenticated propose endpoint behind it; the bind is now loopback unless the operator opts in

the subset enumeration materializes 2^n pairs before the product check that is supposed to refuse it can run, and 2^20 already exceeds MAX_SPLIT_COMBINATIONS, so the bound can never prevent the work it names; measured at 15.9 GB RSS and 38 s of uncharged CPU from a 217-byte deploy

column10: a negative phlo_limit credited the deployer's vault: the charge is a debit and the subtraction inverted. Read as part of the C109 fix; the vault arithmetic, the staking credit and the untrust revocation in this file were reviewed, the rest of the file's native surface was not
the multi-signature vault name was wired to the single-signer rev_vault handler; it now refuses rather than silently providing weaker custody

the only installed logger prints level, class and message with no wall-clock time, debug and trace are empty bodies and is_trace_enabled is hardcoded false, so incident forensics are ordering-only and cross-node timelines cannot be reconstructed from the logs
the no-hash default reads the non-finalized chain tip, so an unauthenticated caller's reads are anchored to a block a byzantine proposer can pick; R19 records this as fixed and it is not

unauthenticated and unrated POST that spends the node's own validator REV to a caller-chosen address, on the wildcard-bound public server; every sibling capability path was hardened and this one was left
the versioned twin of the same tip read on the same unauthenticated route
the versioned twin of the same unauthenticated fund-moving route, mounted from the same handler on the same wildcard-bound public router

mutation sweep: making every node hash alike made this witness FAIL (loudly, at the tree's own internal assertion), so it catches a degenerate mechanism and not merely a structural property. The tree's child maps are BTreeMaps, so order-independence is also structural; the mutation shows the test is not resting on that alone

the row's declared Rust witness cannot fail on this mechanism while its own `falsifiable` prose names the two tests that can: neutering `check_replay_data` to `Ok` unconditionally (`if data.is_empty()` → `if true`) leaves `law11_a_replayed_script_matches_its_recording` GREEN and reddens `a_rig_whose_comm_never_happens_is_reported` (3 passed, 1 failed), which no row names. Cause: the checker reports only rigged events the replay never produced, never missing ones, so the failing shape needs a rig that expects an absent match — the property test replays a script against its own recording and cannot build that. Owed: the two side tests belong in `laws.tsv`/`Laws.lean`/`LAWS.md` column 14, as a three-file change

mutation sweep: relaxing the supermajority gate from `stake * 3 > total_stake * 2` to `>=`, so exactly two thirds counts, turned ALL THREE declared witnesses red — `law14_super_majority_is_strictly_more_than_two_thirds` and `law14_the_two_thirds_boundary_survives_past_the_f64_mantissa` in rchain-sdk, and `law14_fringe_requires_supermajority` in rchain-block-storage. The strongest row swept so far: one mutation, three witnesses, two crates, and the boundary arm is what catches the off-by-one direction

mutation sweep: flipping `m.sender_seq > curr.sender_seq` to `<`, so the layer keeps the minimum sender_seq per sender instead of the maximum, turned the declared witness `calculate_next_layer_picks_max_sender_seq` FAILED, plus one the row does not name (`the_fringe_walk_is_bounded_by_the_non_finalized_chain_length`). Scope: the max-selection was mutated; `check_min_messages_needs_all_bonded_senders`, the row's other declared witness, did not fail under this mutation and was not separately exercised
both named witnesses assert a one-directional property and stay green when add_block_to_dag_state never adds anything; six tests catch it, five of them law 18's, and none belongs to law 15
mutation sweep: accepting any block number turned 2 witnesses red. The descent bound added by H1b is in the same function and was not separately mutated
mutation sweep: accepting any sequence number turned 2 witnesses red

mutation sweep: disabling the sort of `justifications` in `to_proto` (`justifications.sort();` commented out) turned the declared witness `law16_to_proto_sorts_justifications` FAILED, confirming the file's own claim that this is the sort no input can make redundant — it builds an unsorted `Vec`, unlike the `bonds`/`rejected_blocks` sorts whose BTreeMap sources are already ordered. That distinction is recorded in the file at `casper_message.rs:1378-1389` and is why only this clause of law 16 is swept here

mutation sweep: reversing the lexicographic comparison in `min_by` (`(ca, a.len(), sa).cmp(&(cb, b.len(), sb))` → `.reverse()`), so the chosen rejection maximises rather than minimises the total cost, turned the declared witness `law17_the_chosen_rejection_minimizes_the_total_cost` FAILED. 3 passed, 1 failed. Scope: the ordering direction was mutated; the size and sorted-set tie-breakers beyond the cost component were not independently removed, and `law17a`'s fourth declared witness was not under the filter

mutation sweep: wrapping_sub in place of the checked subtraction turned 2 witnesses red. The row's note records that the Scala oracle wraps and this is a deliberate deviation, so the witness is what keeps the deviation honest

mutation sweep: deleting the contiguity check made the two negative witnesses FAIL and left the positive ones green, which is the correct split. The empty-DAG and missing-lowest-height cases were not separately mutated

third instance of the C152/C153 pointer class, and the row whose subject makes it most visible: the statement claims the `Blake2b512Random` merge is n-ary and order-sensitive, and the four declared witnesses are the seed case plus three known-answer vectors for signatures and encryption. Making every child write to the same slot (`finalize_internal(…, i * 32)` → `…, 0`) so only the last contributes leaves all four declared witnesses green and reddens `merge_with_two_children` and `merge_with_many_children`. `merge_is_order_sensitive` (`:548`) also carries a claim the column omits. Owed: the three-file column widening, with C152 and C153
the row's first named witness cannot fail if sorting is deleted, because idempotence is what identity has; the row is still covered by its sibling witness, which does fail
mutation sweep: replacing sort_pars with its input made this witness FAIL, so it is a real falsifier. Only the collection sort was mutated; the arithmetic of the comparison itself was not

a constant Hash for Sorted leaves both law-2 witnesses and all 168 models tests green: the assertion is one-directional (equal implies same hash), which a constant function satisfies. Nothing anywhere asserts the converse. Scope: impl Hash for Sorted is reached only by a test helper, so no consensus path is at risk

mutation sweep: replacing the path-ordered insert with an append (`partition_point(..)` → `entries.len()`) so claims queue by arrival rather than DFS path turned `law20_per_channel_path_order` FAILED, so the row's declared witness is a real falsifier for the ordering. Scope: the whole ordering was mutated; the `<=` tie rule, which is law 24's S.3 window rather than law 20's order, was not independently changed

the declared witness is vacuous on this tree and the cause is the fixture's runtime, not its assertion: deleting the gate's predecessor-await chain leaves it GREEN because `compare_mode` builds a single-threaded runtime where ungated spawns are still polled in spawn order. Swapping in 4 worker threads with the gate still deleted turns it red 3 of 3, and the runtime swap alone passes — so the gate is real and was unobservable. FIXED in `compare_mode`; law 25's witness, which shares the helper, was re-run under the new runtime and passes

mutation sweep: making the concurrent branch drop its resolved terms (`for h in handles` → `for h in handles.into_iter().take(0)`) so no effects are assembled turned the declared witness `law22_the_next_step_closure_is_computable_at_dispatch` FAILED, on its `effects.len() == n` arm. Scope: the assembly was mutated; the second half of the law — that dispatch touches no tuple space — was not independently deleted, and the `i16::MAX` arity guard is not reached by a witness that stops at six terms

mutation sweep: removing Comm::apply's produce sort made this witness FAIL, so it catches the mechanism its own law is about — unlike law 8's witness, which covers the same function but is filed under the selection. The candidate rotation is the test's own construction and was not varied
mutation sweep: disabling the validation gate outright made this witness FAIL. The single gate was mutated; the record-layer half of the law was not independently deleted

the declared witness is vacuous for this mechanism, and the mode→flag switch is covered by nothing: replacing `set_validation_enabled(mode == EffectMode::RelaxedValidated)` with `false` at `rholang/src/reduce.rs:2323` leaves all 250 rholang and all 292 casper lib tests green (counted, not assumed), including this row's own witness. Law 24's witness does catch the queue's validation, but it sets the flag directly on its own queue and so skips the mode switch; `reduce.rs:2323` is the only production site that enables it. Cause is the input distribution as much as the row: `arb_program`'s shapes are confluent under reordering, so a validated/unvalidated comparison cannot separate them — CLOSED in part: `law24_the_effect_mode_is_what_enables_the_certificate` (`5ee8155be`) now witnesses the mode→certificate wiring, re-measured here as `250 passed; 1 failed` under the same plant. Law 25's own declared witness is still green under it, so the row's evidence now exists in the tree, filed under law 24

mutation sweep: disabling the ASCII check in `ShardId::try_from` (`if !v.is_ascii()` → `if false`), so a non-ASCII shard id is admitted, turned the declared witness `law26_a_shard_id_is_accepted_exactly_when_nonempty_ascii` FAILED. Scope: the predicate's second conjunct was mutated; the non-empty conjunct was not, and the row's three other declared witnesses (the two http leg-validation tests and `law26_invalid_shard_names_are_refused`) were not run under this plant

the same three-file column change as C152 is owed for a different row: the declared Rust witnesses are the two end-to-end 2PC integration tests, and deleting the `!self.legs.is_empty()` conjunct from `decision_is_deterministic` leaves both green while reddening `law27_a_legless_record_cannot_commit` — a test that puts the law number in its own name and that no register field mentions. Scope: one guard of the row's several was mutated; the abort-prevents-commit and votes-agree witnesses were not independently deleted

mutation sweep: the row has TWO independent guards — an explicit balance comparison and the NonNegI64 refinement — and removing either alone leaves the witness GREEN because the other still refuses. Removing both makes it FAIL. Single-site mutation cannot fail this witness and that is correct behaviour, not weakness: the overdraw is genuinely still rejected. Verified by removing both

mutation sweep: making the terminal guard in `record_vote` never fire (`if self.state.is_terminal()` → `if false`), so a decided record accepts further votes, turned the declared witness `law29_a_terminal_record_never_changes_again` FAILED. Scope: the absorbing-state guard was deleted; the legless guard in `decision_is_deterministic` was mutated separately under law 27 and did not affect this witness
both named witnesses survive a substitution that does nothing, so the row's evidence is vacuous; four tests it does not name catch the mutation, and none of them is named by any law row

mutation sweep: making the ground-pattern short-circuit answer every target turned the row's declared Rust witness `law5_a_ground_pattern_matches_only_itself` FAILED, so the port-side evidence is real. Scope: only the short-circuit was mutated — the set/map length guard and the remainder arms, which the Lean side names, were not independently deleted
mutation sweep: making every block an epoch boundary turned 2 of the row's 3 witnesses red. The off-boundary arm is the one that carries it; the reward-split witnesses were not independently mutated
mutation sweep: forcing the epoch divisor to 1 (every block a boundary) turned 2 witnesses red. Law 46 shares the pot-split witness and was not separately mutated

the row's declared witness was vacuous and both sides are now fixed: the fixture bonded 4 and 5 against `minimum_bond: 3`, so `bond / minimum_bond` was 1 for every validator and deleting the factor left `an_epoch_splits_the_pot_and_keeps_the_dust` GREEN (law 47's witness caught it). Bonds are now `[4, 8]` — shares 2 and 5, sum 7 of a pot of 10, three units of dust — and the Lean twin `the_dust_is_real` moved to the same instance, since it carried the identical degeneracy over `[4, 5]` and its doc-comment stated that degeneracy as its evidence of strictness. C149 carries both halves; law 45's `falsifiable` prose described the same fixture and moved with it
mutation sweep: both an immediate deadline and an unstaged withdrawal turned 3 witnesses red, so the row is falsified from two directions
mutation sweep: disabling the consume-storage refund made this witness FAIL. The produce-removal refund in the same function was not separately mutated

mutation sweep: replacing the consumed continuation's body with an empty par (`TaggedContinuation::ParBody(body.clone())` → a `ParWithDefault` body in the sequential `.consume` arm) turned the declared witness `peek_and_persistent_work` FAILED, so a receive does reduce to its own body rather than to nothing. Scope: the sequential `consume` arm was mutated; the path-addressed `consume_at` twin at `reduce.rs:2902` was not independently changed, and `list_channel_matches`, the row's other witness, was under a filter that did not run it

mutation sweep: making a fresh name a constant (`let bytes = rand.next()` → a fixed 32-byte vector while still advancing the RNG) turned the declared witness `law4_new_allocates_fresh_names_and_the_reduct_is_closed` FAILED on its `assert_ne!(ids[0], ids[1])` arm — the freshness, not the closedness half. Scope: the allocation was mutated; the closedness assertion is carried by the same test and was not separately targeted

mutation sweep: turning the linearity refusal into a fall-through turned `law5_a_pattern_that_binds_a_variable_twice_never_matches` FAILED while its sibling `law5_a_pattern_that_binds_distinct_variables_matches` stayed green — so the negative arm carries the law and the positive control is not collaterally broken. Scope: only the refusal was mutated; `par_set` canonicalisation and the `.._` remainder arms were not

mutation sweep: removing the parser's recursion guard alone fails only rejects_excessive_nesting_depth, which no law row names — and that is CORRECT, because the row's own witness is named for the composition: with BOTH guards off, rejects_a_deep_ast_that_stays_inside_both_component_guards fails as its name says. A two-guard row where neither half alone is sufficient, like law 28

mutation sweep: a walk that never exceeds anything made this witness FAIL, caught by its one-past-the-limit arm. A first attempt that neutered the ASSERTION rather than the mechanism proved nothing and is recorded here as the trap it is: weakening a test's own claim is not a mutation of the code

mutation sweep: an is_closed that answers true for everything turned 2 witnesses red, caught by the row's negative arm (an open term must NOT be closed). A predicate with only its positive arm would have been vacuous

mutation sweep: removing the sort in hash_hashes left the witness GREEN and that is correct — hash_seq sorts the same hashes upstream, so the mutation removed a redundant duplicate rather than the mechanism. A mutation masked by a second implementation is not a deletion
the registered witness covers Comm::apply's produce sort but not the content-addressed selection; the selector is covered by space_matcher's own test, which no law row names

mutation sweep: a left-projection combine made the monoid witness FAIL, so it is a real falsifier — the two identity assertions are what catch it. The row's other two witnesses are about StateChange::combine and were not mutated

the ledger's own machinery. No adversarial review of the ledger itself yet; check 15 is the mechanical half only, and it is this unit's own output — the pass that reviews the instruments has not run against it.

coverage.yml declares no permissions block, so it runs with the repository default token scope, and resolves five floating action refs of which dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable is a moving branch; it triggers on every push to dev and main, and the hardening the other workflows got is half-applied

authored 2026-09-27 to replace a hand-typed sweep that twice left a live plant in the tree. Read end to end because I wrote it; NOT falsified — nobody has planted a defect in the harness itself and required it to notice, so it is `deferred` and not `cleared`. What it does not do: it cannot stop a concurrent session's `cargo test` from compiling a planted tree during the window the plant is on disk (one test run long), and its `--old` match is exact-string, so a plant that compiles but changes nothing would report a vacuous witness

the anchor check's cited window is the range padded by eight lines on each side, so a citation that moves by up to eight lines still contains the construct it names and is reported ok — measured when cargo fmt --all moved validate.rs by +4 and native_state.rs by +8 and fourteen of seventeen citations pointed at changed content while the step printed ok. The same blindness caught this row's author: one of the fourteen (native_state.rs:2628, law 28's test, moved to :2662) was missed by the hand-built enumeration and fixed a commit later than the other thirteen, with the gate green for it throughout. Read in full: the window construction, the identifier test and the comment that claims moved lines are caught. Not read: the pointer family and coverage-ledger steps of the same script, and the Rchain/LawsMain.lean anchor checks on the other side

the witness verdict matches 'test <name> ...' without requiring '... ok', so libtest's '... ignored' line counts as a pass and an #[ignore]d test satisfies the law register's Rust half; demonstrated live with a witness that panics if it ever runs
